name: vLLM
tagline: vLLM is a high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs
description: vLLM is a high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs. Open-source software; the repository lists the licence as Apache-2.0.
features: High-throughput LLM inference and serving engine
useCases: Serving open models on your own GPUs
strengths: Source code and licence are public in the official repository
No licence fee for the software itself
limitations: You run and maintain it yourself, so hosting, hardware and support costs are your own
We have not run or benchmarked it

openSource.note: The official repository lists the licence as Apache-2.0

free.details: The software is free to use under its Apache-2.0 licence; infrastructure and any hosted offerings are separate.

plans.name: Self-hosted (open source)
plans.note: Free software under the Apache-2.0 licence; your own hosting and hardware costs apply

pricing.regional: No vendor price list. Any hosted or commercial offering from the same team is priced separately and is not covered here.

profile.headline: Fast, easy serving of large language models

capabilities.title: Serve models with high throughput
capabilities.text: State-of-the-art throughput using PagedAttention, continuous batching, chunked prefill and prefix caching.

capabilities.title: Run many model types
capabilities.text: 200+ Hugging Face architectures, from decoder-only and mixture-of-experts models to multimodal, embedding and reward models.

capabilities.title: Fit models on your hardware
capabilities.text: Quantisation including FP8, INT8, INT4, GPTQ, AWQ and GGUF, and several forms of parallelism.

capabilities.title: Expose a standard API
capabilities.text: An OpenAI-compatible server, plus an Anthropic Messages API and gRPC.

featureCards.name: Speculative decoding
featureCards.text: n-gram, suffix, EAGLE and DFlash methods.

featureCards.name: Wide hardware support
featureCards.text: NVIDIA and AMD GPUs and several CPUs, with plugins for TPUs, Gaudi and other accelerators.

featureCards.name: Open community
featureCards.text: Started at UC Berkeley and maintained by many institutions and over 2,000 contributors.

scenarios.title: Run a large mixture-of-experts model
scenarios.text: Split it across GPUs with expert and tensor parallelism.

scenarios.title: Return JSON that follows a schema
